title: Using AI to trade 10 thousand dollars, here’s the results so far
author: Unfair_Set_355
selftext:
Robinhood agentic account: $10,728.87, up $98.17 (up 0.93%) today. We’re 2 weeks in right now (+$728.87), loving how easy it was to get this going, just chose some agents and let it run!

Business As Usual cashed out its weather trade. It holds the S&P 500 and switches into UPRO, a 3x leveraged S&P fund, on days New York weather reads normal for the season on Kalshi's temperature markets. Monday was one of those days. It bought UPRO at $151.47 and sold it this morning at $155.96, +2.96% on the levered leg in one day, about $76. It's back in plain SPY. It still finished today up $23.69 (up 0.90%), the best dollar day in the account.

AI Picks & Shovels, up $21.37 (up 1.99%), and it finally took profit on SMCI. It sold most of the position at $43.51. It first bought SMCI on day 1 at $39.18, so that's about +11% over the series. It also added to Marvell at $288.68. It had bought Marvell the day before at $270.10, so that tranche was already up almost 7% overnight.

FAANG+ Momentum, up $16.21 (up 0.64%). It sold AAPL, META and NVDA and put about $1,100 into NFLX at $67.67. It tried NFLX two weeks ago at $71.49 and sold the next day at $71.57. Round two is coming in about 5% cheaper.

High Profile Congress, up $3.74 (up 0.80%), first green day on the new set of disclosure picks from Monday's rebuild.

The Contrarian sold XLI, the industrials ETF, and bought XLRE, real estate. It buys whichever S&P sectors have been weakest over the last three months, betting they bounce. Real estate is the current loser, so in it goes.

Pelosi Tracker sold TEM and VST and added AAPL, AB, AMZN, GOOGL and INTC off her latest disclosed buys.

comments.author: socialwhizca
comments.body:
The reason every review feels controversial is that all the subjective sources are gameable, paid YouTubers, flooded review sites, divisive Reddit takes. So the trick isn't finding a better opinion, it's switching to things you can verify yourself.



Two objective checks beat any review. First, regulation you confirm, not claim. Take the license number and check it on the actual regulator's site (FCA, ASIC, CySEC, Central Bank of Ireland), not the broker's marketing page. Second, the withdrawal test. Deposit small, trade a bit, pull it out before committing real size. A completed withdrawal is the one thing nobody can fake.



One flag on the Exness bonus you mentioned. Be careful, bonuses are usually a red flag, not a perk. Serious regulators actually restrict or ban deposit bonuses for retail because they push overtrading, so a broker leaning on a bonus program is often telling you something about its regulation. Never pick a broker for a bonus, the withdrawal conditions attached usually trap your money.



For what it's worth, prefer brokers regulated across multiple serious jurisdictions since you can verify them independently (AvaTrade for example, checkable in more than one registry). The deposit-approval delays you hit are normal KYC and not really the thing to judge on, the real question is what happens when you try to take money OUT, not put it in. Verify the license, test a withdrawal, ignore the bonuses.
